AngleX.description: Set the routed Live Control destination's X-axis rotation angle in degrees, without changing Y or Z. Companion to AngleDelta (relative shift). Writes `Master.RotoAngleX` (not `Master.AngleX` as the property name suggests). Range `[-2880, +2880]` (i.e. ±8 full rotations); values outside silently clamp to the bound. No modulo-360 wraparound - `AngleX 720` stores 720 verbatim. Negatives accepted.

verification.verificationScript: ControlMaster / AngleX 45 / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "f", Master.RotoAngleX ; AngleX 12345 / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "f", Master.RotoAngleX
verification.expectedCallback: Property write confirmed: `AngleX 45` set Master.RotoAngleX = 45 (Master.AngleX stayed at 0). Each axis is independent (AngleX leaves RotoAngleY/Z untouched). Range verified: values in [-2880, +2880] pass through verbatim including negatives and multi-rotation values (`AngleX 720` → 720, no modulo wrap). Values outside clamp to ±2880: `AngleX 2881` → 2880, `AngleX 10000` → 2880, `AngleX -10000` → -2880.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.RotoAngleX baseline; run AngleX -2881, -2880, 12.5, 2880, and 2881 as bounded writes; read Master.RotoAngleX after each write; restore baseline with AngleX 0.

AnimateProp.description: Schedule a linear animation of a numeric property from startValue to finishValue over durationMS milliseconds. Optional finishEvent fires PulseEvent at end-of-animation. Animations run on a dedicated BEYOND thread at about 40 FPS resolution.

forms.description: Linear animation of a named numeric property from start to finish over duration (ms).

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: Full dotted property path (e.g. "Master.Brightness"). Must be numeric.

parameters.name: startValue
parameters.range: target-property-dependent numeric value

valueRange.notes: BEYOND readback probe on 2026-05-11 animated Master.Brightness from 100 to 90 and confirmed the target property reached 90. The accepted value range is determined by the target property, not by AnimateProp itself.

parameters.description: Starting value at t=0. Valid range is determined by the target property.

parameters.name: finishValue
parameters.range: target-property-dependent numeric value

valueRange.notes: BEYOND readback probe on 2026-05-11 animated Master.Brightness from 100 to 90 and confirmed the target property reached 90. The accepted value range is determined by the target property, not by AnimateProp itself.

parameters.description: Final value at t=durationMS. Valid range is determined by the target property.

parameters.name: durationMS
parameters.range: 0 and positive milliseconds observed; upper bound not established

valueRange.notes: BEYOND readback probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed duration 0 completes immediately, duration 250 completes a short animation, and duration 60000 starts a long animation that can be cancelled with DeletePropAni. No maximum duration was established.

parameters.description: Duration in milliseconds. Zero completes immediately; positive durations animate over time.

parameters.name: finishEvent
parameters.range: free-form event name; empty string accepted
parameters.description: Optional event name to fire at end-of-animation, equivalent to PulseEvent. A named event string and an empty string parse and do not prevent the animation from completing.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.Brightness baseline; run AnimateProp "Master.Brightness", 100, 90, 250; read Master.Brightness; run AnimateProp "Master.Brightness", 100, 95, 0; read Master.Brightness; run AnimateProp "Master.Brightness", 100, 99, 60000; read Master.Brightness; cancel with DeletePropAni "Master.Brightness" and restore with ControlMaster / Brightness 100.
verification.expectedCallback: BEYOND readback probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed 250 ms animation reached 90, 0 ms animation completed immediately at 95, and 60000 ms animation began interpolating then was cancelled. Restore readback returned Master.Brightness to 100.

verification.verificationScript: Run AnimateProp "Master.Brightness", 100, 98, 100, "PangoLintAnimDone" then AnimateProp "Master.Brightness", 100, 99, 100, ""; read Master.Brightness after each; restore with ControlMaster / Brightness 100.
verification.expectedCallback: Named finishEvent and empty-string finishEvent both allowed the animation to complete. Event delivery was not observed directly in this probe.

propertyMappingCoverage.notes: Dynamic property-path argument command. It writes whichever numeric property string is supplied at runtime, so PangoLint cannot publish a fixed setsProperty target.

AnimatePropDelta.description: Schedule a linear animation that shifts a numeric property by totalDelta over durationMS milliseconds. Starting value is the property's current value at task-creation time. Optional finishEvent fires PulseEvent at end-of-animation.

forms.description: Relative-shift animation: shift a named numeric property by totalDelta over duration (ms).

parameters.range: target-property-dependent numeric delta

parameters.name: durationMS
parameters.range: 0 and positive milliseconds observed; upper bound not established

valueRange.notes: BEYOND readback probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed AnimatePropDelta with duration 0 shifted Master.Brightness from 100 to 99, and duration 250 shifted it from 100 to approximately 95. No maximum duration was established.

parameters.description: Duration in milliseconds. Zero completes immediately; positive durations animate over time.

BeamBrush.description: Set the routed Live Control destination's BeamBrush parameter (laser line width). BEYOND documentation says: 'Set BeamBrush value (laser line width).' Writes `Master.BeamBrush`, range `[0, 100]` with silent clamp on both ends (negative values clamp to 0; values above 100 clamp to 100). Companion: `BeamBrushDelta` for relative shift. BEYOND documentation examples: `BeamBrush 0` (sharp line), `BeamBrush 25` (1/4 width), `BeamBrush 100` (widest).

Out-of-range silent clamp confirmed: BeamBrush -1 -> 0, BeamBrush 101 -> 100, BeamBrush 1000 -> 100. Float precision preserved (BeamBrush 99.99 -> 99.989...). BeamBrushDelta verified to add to current value: BeamBrush 50 then BeamBrushDelta 7 -> 57.

ColorBGR.description: Set the color used for **live frame recoloring** in the Live Control RGB section. BEYOND documentation says: 'Sets the color used for live frame recoloring. The color value is a 24-bit unsigned integer.' Same target family as `ColorRGB`; the difference is byte ordering. **BGR encoding** (high byte = Red in Master readback): with baseline `RGBA 1, 2, 3, 4`, `ColorBGR 1122867` (`0x112233`) set `Master.Red` to 17 and updated packed `Master.RGBColor`, while Green/Blue/Alpha stayed unchanged. Use `ColorOn 1` to enable the recolor (sets alpha 255); `ColorOn 0` disables (alpha 0).

forms.description: Set the live-recolor color in BGR-packed 24-bit format.

parameters.name: packedColor

valueRange.notes: Fresh MCP write/read probe on 2026-05-12 confirmed ColorBGR applies the high byte of the lower 24-bit value to Master.Red in the current Master route while Green and Blue stay unchanged from baseline: 257, 511, and 512 read Red=0; 0x1FFFF read Red=1; 0xFF0000FF read Red=0. This is byte masking, not clamp behavior. PangoLint lint acceptance was not used as runtime proof because this data set is still being filled in.

parameters.description: Packed 24-bit color, BGR-ordered (high RGB byte affects Master.Red in the current Master route). E.g. 0x0000FF = pure blue, 0xFF0000 = pure red. Use `ColorOn 1` to apply the recolor.

verification.notes: 2026-05-11 BEYOND readback: baseline RGBA 1/2/3/4, then ColorBGR 1122867 (0x112233) produced Master.Red=17, Master.Green=2, Master.Blue=3, Master.Alpha=4, Master.RGBColor=197137. Confirms writable paths Master.Red and packed Master.RGBColor in the Master route.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.Red/Green/Blue/Alpha/RGBColor baseline; from RGBA 0,0,0,4 run ColorBGR 257, 511, 512, 0x1FFFF, and 0xFF0000FF with readback after each; restore the captured baseline.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP write/read probe on 2026-05-12 confirmed ColorBGR 257, 511, and 512 read back Red=0 with Green=0 and Blue=0; ColorBGR 0x1FFFF read back Red=1; ColorBGR 0xFF0000FF read back Red=0. Packed RGBColor followed the changed Red byte. Restore used the captured baseline, which was 255/255/255/0 in this run, and readback returned to 255/255/255/0. PangoLint lint acceptance was not used as runtime proof because this data set is still being filled in.

ColorOn.description: Enable or disable the **Live Control RGB recoloring** by setting the alpha channel. BEYOND documentation says: 'Enables laser frame recoloring using the Live Control RGB section. This command specifically sets the Alpha channel to either 0 or 255 - a simple on/off control for alpha.' Pairs with `ColorRGB` / `ColorBGR` which set the recolor color. Numeric values behave as a threshold: values <= 0 set alpha 0, values > 0 set alpha 255. Symbolic OFF and ON are accepted.

parameters.name: enabled

valueRange.notes: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed ColorOn -1 and 0 set Master.Alpha=0, while 0.5, 1, and 2 set Master.Alpha=255. Symbolic OFF and ON are also accepted.

parameters.description: Enable threshold. Standard values are 0/OFF and 1/ON; runtime treats values <= 0 as OFF and values > 0 as ON.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.Alpha baseline; from RGBA 1,2,3,4 run ColorOn -1, 0, 0.5, 1, 2, OFF, and ON with Master.Alpha readback after each; restore baseline with RGBA 255, 255, 255, 0.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed ColorOn -1 and ColorOn 0 read back Master.Alpha=0; ColorOn 0.5, 1, and 2 read back Master.Alpha=255. Symbolic ColorOn OFF read back 0 and ColorOn ON read back 255. Restore returned Master.Alpha to 0.

v = Master.ColorSlider

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.ColorSlider baseline; run ColorSlider 0.1, 0.4, 0.5, 0.6, 0.9, 1.5, 254.5, and 255.5 with readback after each; restore baseline with ColorSlider 0.

Brightness 60

Brightness 65

Brightness 70
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against Master.Brightness, MasterLC.Brightness, and ActGridFocusedCue.Brightness in BEYOND 2030 (LC tab focused on Master). Baseline: Master=62, MasterLC=62, ActGridFocusedCue=100. After ControlFromUI+60: Master=60, MasterLC=60. After ControlFromLcTab+65: Master=65, MasterLC=65. After ControlMaster+70 (control case): Master=70, MasterLC=70. Master and MasterLC always co-vary (likely aliased or shadow-linked). All three commands routed to the same destination - ControlFromUI and ControlFromLcTab are observationally equivalent in this state, consistent with the Wiki's deprecation note. Equivalence across other LC-tab destinations (cue / zone / ProTrack) is inferred from the symmetric routing behavior here.

ControlProTrack.description: Bind the calling script's Live Control routing register to a specific ProTrack by 1-based index. Only one ProTrack can be addressed at a time; use ControlSelProTracks to fan out to a selection. The cap is **1..8 hard** - `ControlProTrack 9` and higher are silently dropped (no parser error, no wrap, no effect). BEYOND's UI confirms only 8 ProTrack slots exist (ProTrack 1..ProTrack 8 tabs) with no UI affordance to add more.

forms.description: Bind this script to an exact ProTrack. Range 1..8; out-of-range values are silently dropped at runtime.

parameters.name: proTrackIndex
parameters.description: 1-based ProTrack index. Hard cap of 8; BEYOND's UI exposes exactly 8 ProTrack slots, and `ControlProTrack 9` or higher routes to nothing (silently dropped, no parser or runtime error). Maps to `ProTrack.<n-1>.<property>` in the BEYOND object tree for readback.

verification.verificationScript:
ControlProTrack 1
Brightness 11
ControlProTrack 8
Brightness 22
ControlProTrack 9
Brightness 33
ControlProTrack 16
Brightness 44
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against `ProTrack.<n>.Brightness` in BEYOND 2030 with the workspace configured at the default 8 ProTracks. Baseline: ProTrack.0..7 = 100. After `ControlProTrack 1 + Brightness 11`: ProTrack.0 = 11. After `ControlProTrack 8 + Brightness 22`: ProTrack.7 = 22. After `ControlProTrack 9 + Brightness 33` and `ControlProTrack 16 + Brightness 44`: no readable property changed - silently dropped. UI inspection confirms BEYOND exposes exactly 8 ProTrack slots (tabs ProTrack 1..ProTrack 8) with no affordance to add more, supporting the hard-cap interpretation. ProTrack.8..11 readbacks returned 0 (likely zero-fill rather than the -1 sentinel seen on DmxOutput out-of-range; further differentiation between 'property exists with value 0' and 'property does not exist' was not pursued in this probe).

ControlSelProTracks.description: Route subsequent Live Control commands to every currently selected ProTrack. Selection state at execution time determines scope. The routing is ProTrack-only - a `ControlSelProTracks` followed by `Brightness 28` writes to the selected ProTrack(s) and leaves selected zones untouched. This is the symmetric counterpart to ControlSelZones - neither command fans out to the other selection set.

ControlSelZones.description: Route subsequent Live Control commands to every currently selected projection zone. BEYOND fans the next Live Control command out as one command per selected zone. Routing is zones-only. A documented claim that this command also addresses selected ProTracks is wrong for current builds. A `ControlSelZones` followed by `Brightness 73` with both a zone and a ProTrack selected wrote only to the zone: Zone.0.Brightness = 73, ProTrack.0.Brightness unchanged at 100. Use ControlSelProTracks separately when you need to address ProTracks.

forms.description: Bind this script to selected zones. Runtime evidence shows zones-only routing and contradicts older documentation that this command also addresses selected ProTracks.

verification.verificationScript:
UnselectAllZones
UnselectAllProTracks
SelectZone 1
SelectProTrack 1
ControlSelZones
Brightness 73
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against `Zone.0.Brightness` and `ProTrack.0.Brightness` in BEYOND 2030. Baseline: Zone.0.Brightness = 100, ProTrack.0.Brightness = 100. After `ControlSelZones / Brightness 73`: Zone.0.Brightness = 73, ProTrack.0.Brightness = 100 (unchanged). After a follow-up `ControlSelProTracks / Brightness 28` with same selection: Zone.0.Brightness = 73 (unchanged), ProTrack.0.Brightness = 28. Confirms ControlSelZones is zones-only and ControlSelProTracks is ProTracks-only. Neither command fans out to the other selection set, refuting the documented `also addresses selected ProTracks` claim.

DmxOut.description: Set a DMX output channel. Range is 1..2048 spanning 4 universes as a flat array. A `DmxOut 600, 128` write reads back as `DmxOutput.599 = 128` (i.e. Universe 2 channel 88 = 128 in flat-array indexing) without wrapping or rejection. The older documented 1..512 cap reflects single-universe configurations historically and is no longer accurate for current 4-universe BEYOND. Use -1 as the value for transparent (yield).

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: DMX value 0..255; -1 means transparent (yield to other sources).

verification.verificationScript:
DmxOut 50, 200
DmxOut 512, 250
DmxOut 600, 128
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP send + OscOutTTS readback against BEYOND 2030 with 4 ArtNet output universes configured. After each write, read back via `var v / v = DmxOutput.<n> / OscOutTTS "/pangolint/probe/<id>", "i", v`: DmxOutput.49 = 200 (write to ch 50 lands at 0-based index 49); DmxOutput.511 = 250 (universe 1 boundary); DmxOutput.599 = 128 (universe 2 channel 88, refuting the documented 1..512 cap); DmxOutput.512 / .600 returned -1 (out-of-bounds sentinel). No wrap-to-universe-1 observed (DmxOutput.87 / .88 stayed at 0). Confirms the Wiki's 1..2048 flat-array model.

Fb4DiscoveryMode.description: Set this BEYOND instance's role in the multi-BEYOND FB4 failover discovery system. Values: 0 = always (continuous claim), 1 = auto (cooperative; default), 2 = manual (passive / wait for failover). Setting mode `1` (auto) is what re-enables discovery after a `StopFb4Discovery` had disabled it; without this step, `StartFb4Discovery` alone won't reconnect. Mode `2` produces the BEYOND notification 'Discovery: Waiting for other BEYOND in network', confirming the failover-passive interpretation. Mode `1` produces the notification 'Discovery: Discovery automatically enabled'.

Hue.description: Set the routed Live Control destination's hue override (a color recolor - replaces the cue's input color hue with this value). BEYOND documentation says: 'Set the Hue component. Negative values treated as not active, and hue has not impact on recolor.' Writes `Master.Hue`. **Special semantics: `-1` (or any negative value below `-1`) means DISABLED** - `Hue -1` reads back -1, `Hue -2` clamps to -1. Active range `[0, 720]` (degrees, allowing 2× wrap) with silent clamp on the upper bound (`Hue 999` → 720). Companion: `HueDelta` for relative shift. Distinct from `HueShift` which oscillates around the existing color rather than replacing it.

verification.verificationScript: ControlMaster / Hue 60 / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "f", Master.Hue
verification.expectedCallback: Prior range probe: Hue 60 -> 60, HueDelta 30 -> 90 (verified relative-add). Disabled sentinel: Hue -1 -> -1 (preserved); Hue -2 -> -1 (clamped to disabled). Upper clamp: Hue 720 -> 720, Hue 720.01 -> 720, Hue 1000 -> 720. Float precision OK (Hue -0.5 -> -0.5, Hue 360 -> 360).

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.Hue baseline; run ControlMaster with Hue -2, -1, -0.5, 0, 360.5, 720, and 721 as bounded writes; read Master.Hue after each write; restore baseline with Hue -1.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed baseline -1. Hue -2 read back -1; -1 read back -1; -0.5 read back -0.5; 0 read back 0; 360.5 read back 360.5; 720 read back 720; 721 read back 720. Restore returned Master.Hue to -1.

forms.description: Set the LiveControl hue override. Use -1 to disable.

parameters.name: value

valueRange.notes: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed values below -1 clamp to -1, fractional values such as -0.5 and 360.5 pass through, and values above 720 clamp to 720. Negative stored values disable the hue override.

parameters.description: Hue value in degrees. Negative stored values disable the hue override; values below -1 clamp to -1. Active hue values 0..720 pass through; above-range values silently clamp to 720. Reads back as Master.Hue.

HueDelta.description: Apply a relative shift to the routed Live Control destination's hue value (degrees). BEYOND documentation says: 'Increment or decrement the Hue property by specified value. This is relative command.' BEYOND documentation example: `HueDelta 5` (shift current hue by 5°). A HueDelta of +30 applied to a baseline of 60 produces 90. Final value still subject to `Master.Hue` constraints (range `[0, 720]` plus the `-1 = disabled` sentinel). Distinct from `HueShiftDelta` which adjusts the oscillation offset rather than the override.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.Hue baseline; run ControlMaster with Hue 60 / HueDelta 30, Hue -1 / HueDelta -1, Hue 720 / HueDelta 1, and Hue 10 / HueDelta 0.5 with readback after each; restore baseline with Hue -1.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed additive delta semantics and resulting clamp: 60 + 30 read back 90; -1 + (-1) read back -1; 720 + 1 read back 720; 10 + 0.5 read back 10.5. Restore returned Master.Hue to -1.

forms.description: Increment or decrement Master.Hue by a delta. Final value subject to range constraints.

parameters.name: delta
parameters.range: relative; result clamps to -1..720

valueRange.notes: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed additive deltas, fractional delta pass-through, and result clamping to -1..720.

parameters.description: Positive or negative hue delta in degrees. Fractional deltas are accepted; the resulting Master.Hue value clamps to -1..720. BEYOND documentation example: HueDelta 5.

HueShift.description: Set the routed Live Control destination's hue-shift offset, which applies a rotation offset to the existing color palette instead of replacing it. BEYOND documentation says: 'Hue shift is an additional offset for the hue value. Made for additional oscillation around current hue. If you need to recolor then use Hue, which replaces the input color Hue.' `Master.HueShift` stores every value from -1000000 to 1000000 without clamp. Companion: `HueShiftDelta`. Distinct from `Hue`: `Hue` replaces the input color's hue, while `HueShift` adds an offset to it.

verification.verificationScript: ControlMaster / HueShift 90 / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "f", Master.HueShift
verification.expectedCallback: Prior range probe: HueShift 90 -> 90, HueShiftDelta 15 -> 105 (verified relative-add). Wide-range sweep showed no clamp observed at boundaries: HueShift -1000 -> -1000, HueShift -721 -> -721, HueShift -719 -> -719, HueShift 719 -> 719, HueShift 720 -> 720, HueShift 721 -> 721, HueShift 1000 -> 1000. The property accumulator is unbounded in the probed span.

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.HueShift baseline; run ControlMaster with HueShift -10000, 10000, -100000, 100000, -1000000, and 1000000; read Master.HueShift after each write; restore baseline with HueShift 0.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-12 confirmed baseline 0. HueShift -10000, 10000, -100000, 100000, -1000000, and 1000000 read back verbatim. Restore returned Master.HueShift to 0.

parameters.range: pass-through; no clamp observed through -1000000..1000000

valueRange.notes: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-12 confirmed -10000, 10000, -100000, 100000, -1000000, and 1000000 pass through. No clamp observed in that span.

parameters.description: Hue-shift offset in degrees. Adds to the existing color hue instead of replacing it. No clamp is documented through -1000000..1000000; values pass through to Master.HueShift. BEYOND documentation example: HueShift 90.

LockScreen.description: Lock the BEYOND application UI. BEYOND documentation says: 'Places BEYOND into a locked state, preventing unauthorized access or unintended changes to the user interface.' Requires a UI-side password set via BEYOND's **Configuration → Security** panel; without it, BEYOND surfaces a notification ('Lock screen: Please set password in Configuration/Security to avoid lockup') and refuses to engage (Status.Locked stays 0). With the UI password set, `LockScreen` engages immediately and `Status.Locked` reads 1. **Important**: the required password is the UI-side one - NOT the PangoScript `Password` command (which is the unrelated TCP Talk Server auth, sourced from BEYOND.INI). Lock state is observable at `Status.Locked` (1 = locked, 0 = unlocked).

forms.description: Lock the BEYOND UI. Requires a UI-side password configured in BEYOND Configuration/Security; the PangoScript Password command is unrelated.

verification.verificationScript: LockScreen / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", Status.Locked ; (after operator sets UI password in Configuration/Security): LockScreen / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", Status.Locked / UnLockScreen / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", Status.Locked
verification.expectedCallback: Three probe rounds: (1) bare LockScreen with no UI password set → Status.Locked stayed 0; BEYOND notification panel showed 'Lock screen: Please set password in Configuration/Security to avoid lockup'. (2) `Password "TestPass" / LockScreen` ALSO left Status.Locked at 0 - confirming the PangoScript Password command is unrelated to the LockScreen feature (it's TCP Talk Server auth per BEYOND documentation). (3) After operator set the LockScreen password to 'TestPass' via BEYOND's Configuration/Security UI, bare LockScreen successfully transitioned Status.Locked from 0 → 1, and bare UnLockScreen (no password supplied) released it back to 0. Notable security finding: script-driven UnLockScreen bypasses the password requirement that UI-side unlock would enforce.

propertyMappingCoverage.notes: With a UI-side lock password configured, runtime readback confirmed LockScreen writes Status.Locked from 0 to 1. Without that UI password, BEYOND refuses to lock and Status.Locked stays 0.

MakeSecuredFile.description: Generate a Pangolin secured file from an input file. Secured files are encrypted and hardware-bound. Call pattern: `MakeSecuredFile "Input file name", "Output file name", ClientHardwareSerial`. The third argument placeholder `ClientHardwareSerial` is **NOT a built-in token**; it is the example name of a regular script variable the operator must declare and assign before calling. Operators must look up their target hardware's serial (e.g. via `Projector.<N>.Serial`) and assign it explicitly: `var Serial / Serial = <hardwareSerial> / MakeSecuredFile "in", "out", Serial`, or pass an integer literal directly.

forms.description: Encrypt input file to output, binding to the supplied hardware serial. The third argument is a regular integer expression (variable or literal), NOT a built-in identifier.

parameters.name: inputPath
parameters.description: Source file path (Windows-absolute).

parameters.name: outputPath
parameters.description: Destination path for the secured output.

parameters.name: clientHardwareSerial
parameters.description: Hardware serial number to bind to. Pass as a regular integer expression: variable or literal. The example placeholder `ClientHardwareSerial` is just a suggested variable name; the operator must declare and assign it. To pull the connected hardware's serial programmatically, read `Projector.<N>.Serial` (device enumeration) or `FB3_<serial>.Serial` / `FB4_<serial>.Serial` (direct device path).

verification.verificationScript: var v / v = ClientHardwareSerial / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", v ; var ClientHardwareSerial / ClientHardwareSerial = <sentinelInteger> / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", ClientHardwareSerial
verification.expectedCallback: Probed without invoking MakeSecuredFile (file-write side effects avoided). (1) Reading `ClientHardwareSerial` as a bare identifier in an expression returned 0 (silent-zero default for undefined identifier) - refutes case (a) 'built-in token resolved at runtime'. (2) Declaring `var ClientHardwareSerial` and assigning a synthetic sentinel integer, then reading it, returned that same sentinel - confirms case (b) regular variable name. The export's example value is a placeholder, NOT a special identifier. Operators wanting to bind to live hardware should use Projector.<N>.Serial as the value source.

MasterShowSpeed.description: Show timeline speed multiplier (Timeline / PlayList mode). **Input is in percent, where 100 = normal speed.** Stored Master.ShowSpeed = input / 100. So `MasterShowSpeed 100` -> 1.0 (normal), `MasterShowSpeed 50` -> 0.5 (half), `MasterShowSpeed 1000` -> 10.0 (10x normal). No upper cap is documented up to input 9999 (stored 99.99). Both the documented `0..1` and the Wiki's `0..10` ranges describe the *stored fractional* range, not the input. The actual input range in current BEYOND is at minimum 0..9999 in percent.

verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against Master.ShowSpeed in BEYOND 2030. Input 100 -> 1 (normal). Input 50 -> 0.5. Input 1000 -> 10. Input 9999 -> 99.99. Confirms input / 100 = stored, with no observed upper cap. Refutes both the Wiki '0..10' and documented '0..1' input range, which are the stored fractional range rather than the input. Same scaling verified for MasterCueSpeed and MasterLCSpeed in the same probe, likely uniform across the per-target Master*Speed family.

verification.expectedCallback: Two-stage probe in BEYOND 2030. (1) Parser shape: the 3-arg form parsed cleanly; 1-arg (`MidiOut 0x90`), 2-arg (`MidiOut 0x90, 0x40`), and 6-arg/SysEx-shaped (`MidiOut 0xF0, 0x7E, 0x7F, 0x06, 0x01, 0xF7`) all triggered 'Code contain errors'. (2) Wire-level via loopMIDI -> Protokol MIDI monitor: `MidiOut 0x90, 0x40, 0x7F` emitted exactly the bytes 90 40 7F (NoteOn ch1 note 64 vel 127). Confirms MidiOut is strictly a fixed 3-byte sender; variable-length / SysEx must use MidiOutLong.

MidiOutLong.description: Send a variable-length MIDI message (1..N bytes) to the script's selected MIDI device. Counterpart to `MidiOut` (which is strictly 3-byte). The byte sequence is sent as-is on the MIDI wire, with no wrapping or padding. Use this for SysEx messages (0xF0..0xF7 framing), 2-byte messages (Program Change 0xC0..0xCF, Channel Pressure 0xD0..0xDF), 1-byte System Real-Time messages (Timing Clock 0xF8, Start 0xFA, Continue 0xFB, Stop 0xFC, etc.), and standard 3-byte channel-voice messages.

forms.description: Send a variable-length MIDI message (1..N bytes) literally on the MIDI wire. Counterpart to MidiOut for messages that aren't exactly 3 bytes - SysEx, 2-byte messages (Program Change, Channel Pressure), 1-byte System Real-Time (clock/start/stop/continue).

parameters.name: bytes
parameters.description: One or more MIDI byte values, each 0..0xFF. The first byte is typically a status byte (0x80..0xFF); for SysEx start with 0xF0 and end with 0xF7. 1, 2, 3, and 6-byte forms parse and emit those exact bytes in order on the MIDI wire.

MidiOutLong 0xC0, 0x05
MidiOutLong 0xF8

verification.expectedCallback: Two-stage probe in BEYOND 2030. (1) Parser shape: the 1-arg, 2-arg, 3-arg, and 6-arg SysEx-shaped forms all parsed cleanly; the same forms on `MidiOut` (except 3-arg) triggered 'Code contain errors'. (2) Wire-level via loopMIDI -> Protokol MIDI monitor: `MidiOutLong 0x90, 0x41, 0x7F` emitted bytes 90 41 7F (NoteOn ch1 note 65 vel 127), `MidiOutLong 0xC0, 0x05` emitted C0 05 (Program Change to program 5), `MidiOutLong 0xF8` emitted F8 (Timing Clock), `MidiOutLong 0xF0, 0x7E, 0x7F, 0x06, 0x01, 0xF7` emitted F0 7E 7F 06 01 F7 (SysEx Identity Request). Confirms MidiOutLong sends the byte sequence literally - no padding, no wrapping.

MIDI feedback bindings are configured per-property in BEYOND's UI (the per-control 'Learn / MIDI message / Enable MIDI feedback' dialog); there is no PangoScript-side `RegisterMidiFeedback` command. With a feedback binding configured on the Live Control Brightness slider, each `ResetMidiFeedback` call emits a single MIDI message per binding carrying the property's current value (e.g. Brightness at 49% emitted DATA2 = 62, consistent with the standard 0..100 -> 0..127 conversion), and the binding survives; slider movements continue to emit feedback after the call.

SetMidiFeedback "test", "Master.Brightness"
verification.expectedCallback: Parser-shape probe in BEYOND 2030 with all four candidate names (RegisterMidiFeedback, MidiFeedback, RegisterMidi, SetMidiFeedback) and a few argument-shape variants. All forms triggered the 'Code contain errors' popup. Confirms there is no PangoScript-side MIDI-feedback registration command. Operator confirmed BEYOND's per-control MIDI feedback configuration dialog (the 'Learn / MIDI message / Enable MIDI feedback' panel) is the only registration surface.

verification.verificationScript: ResetMidiFeedback
verification.expectedCallback: Wire-level probe in BEYOND 2030 with loopMIDI + Protokol. Operator first configured a MIDI feedback binding on the Live Control Brightness slider via BEYOND's UI (status byte 0x80, data1 0x00, data2 = current slider value), confirmed the binding by moving the slider and seeing Protokol receive matching messages. Then `ResetMidiFeedback` was sent via Talk UDP. Protokol received exactly one MIDI message carrying the slider's current value as DATA2 (Brightness at 49% -> DATA2 = 62, matching the 0..100 -> 0..127 conversion). The binding survived the call - subsequent slider movements continued to emit feedback. Confirms ResetMidiFeedback is a force-resend (not a deregistration) and parallels ResetOscFeedback's verified behavior on the MIDI bus.

Saturation.description: Set the routed Live Control destination's saturation OFFSET. BEYOND documentation says: 'Sets saturation level of the current Live Control. Saturation is not direct value. In Live Control it works as an offset. Incoming color transformed to HSV, modified and transformed back.' Writes `Master.Saturation`, range `[-100, 100]` with silent clamp on both ends. **Saturation is signed**: 0 means no offset (no change), negative values reduce saturation (toward grey), positive values increase saturation. Companion: `SaturationDelta`.

verification.verificationScript: ControlMaster / Saturation 40 / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "f", Master.Saturation
verification.expectedCallback: Prior range probe: Saturation 40 -> 40, SaturationDelta 10 -> 50 (verified relative-add). Range sweep: Saturation -100 -> -100, Saturation -99 -> -99, Saturation 0 -> 0, Saturation 99 -> 99, Saturation 100 -> 100. Clamp confirmed: Saturation -101 -> -100, Saturation 101 -> 100, Saturation 200 -> 100. Default value 0.

SetBpm.description: Set the master BPM tempo. Affects every beat-synced cue, effect, and script reading the Timer beat. Range is **1..600** with hard clamping at both ends. Older `0.1..600` range labels are right on the upper bound but wrong on the lower; values <= 0 and 0.1 are clamped to 1, not accepted as-is. Values > 600 are clamped to 600.

verification.verificationScript:
SetBpm 0.1
SetBpm 1
SetBpm 200
SetBpm 400
SetBpm 600
SetBpm 601
SetBpm 700
SetBpm 1000
SetBpm -1
SetBpm 0
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against Master.BPM in BEYOND 2030. Lower-clamp inputs (-1, 0, 0.1) all produced Master.BPM = 1 (clamped to floor of 1). In-range values (1, 60, 120, 200, 399, 400, 401, 499, 500, 600) all passed through to the same readback value. Upper-clamp inputs (601, 700, 1000) all produced Master.BPM = 600 (clamped to ceiling of 600). Confirms hard clamping at both ends, with the verified range being 1..600 (Wiki's 0.1 lower bound was off - actual floor is 1).

verification.verificationScript: Read Master.BPM baseline; run SetBpm -1, 0, 0.1, 1, 120, 600, 601, and 1000 one at a time via Talk UDP; read Master.BPM after each write; restore the baseline.
verification.expectedCallback: Fresh MCP probe on 2026-05-11 confirmed: baseline 120; -1, 0, and 0.1 read back as 1; 1 read back as 1; 120 read back as 120; 600 read back as 600; 601 and 1000 read back as 600; restore readback returned to 120.

SetCueCaptionColor.description: Set the caption background color of an individual cue cell. BEYOND documentation describes the color as GDI format, where 0x0000FF is red. SetCueCaptionColor stores the supplied packed integer at WS.N.N.CaptionColor without byte swapping, but readback alone does not prove the visual color channel meaning. Pages and cells are 1-based for writable cue locations. UI annotation only; no laser-output effect. Caption colors can persist with workspace save.

forms.description: Set caption background color of a specific cue cell. Color uses documented GDI RGB encoding.

parameters.name: page
parameters.range: 1-based workspace page index; pages 1 and 2 observed in lab, page 0 no-op, pages 3, 9, 10, and 11 had no matching WS readback change in this workspace

valueRange.notes: SetCueCaptionColor page N maps to WS.(N-1).<cell-1>.CaptionColor for pages that exist. The lab workspace wrote pages 1 and 2. Page 0, 3, 9, 10, and 11 transmissions produced no matching WS readback change, so the upper bound is workspace-dependent.

parameters.description: 1-based workspace page index. The maximum page depends on the loaded workspace.

parameters.name: cell
parameters.range: 1-based cue cell index; cells 1, 9, 10, 11, 60, and 61 observed; cell 0 no-op; upper bound not established

valueRange.notes: The lab workspace wrote cell 1 to WS.N.0, cell 9 to WS.N.8, cell 10 to WS.N.9, cell 11 to WS.N.10, cell 60 to WS.N.59, and cell 61 to WS.N.60. Cell 0 produced no WS.0.0 change. No upper bound was established.

parameters.description: 1-based cell index within the page. The workspace accepted cell values beyond 10; do not infer a 10-cell maximum.

parameters.name: packedColor
parameters.range: 0x000000..0xFFFFFF documented GDI RGB color; 0xFFFFFFFF stores as signed -1; visual alpha/reset behavior unverified

valueRange.notes: BEYOND docs describe the parameter as GDI format where 0x0000FF is red. Runtime readback stored 0x000000 as 0, 0x0000FF as 255, 0x00FF00 as 65280, 0xFF0000 as 16711680, 0xFFFFFF as 16777215, and 0xFFFFFFFF as signed -1. Readback confirms stored integer values, not visual channel rendering.

acceptedValues.label: Red, documented GDI RGB low byte
Blue, documented GDI RGB high byte
Observed readback as signed -1; visual alpha or reset behavior unverified

parameters.description: Packed color in documented GDI RGB encoding. Readback preserves the supplied integer, but visual channel meaning comes from BEYOND documentation rather than readback alone.

verification.verificationScript: Read baseline WS caption colors; write SetCueCaptionColor 1,1 with 0x000000, 0x0000FF, 0x00FF00, 0xFF0000, 0xFFFFFF, and 0xFFFFFFFF; probe page values 0, 1, 2, 3, 9, 10, 11 and cell values 0, 1, 9, 10, 11, 60, 61; restore changed cells.
verification.expectedCallback: SetCueCaptionColor 1,1 stored 0x000000 as 0, 0x0000FF as 255, 0x00FF00 as 65280, 0xFF0000 as 16711680, 0xFFFFFF as 16777215, and 0xFFFFFFFF as signed -1 at WS.0.0.CaptionColor. Page 1 cell 1 mapped to WS.0.0 and page 2 cell 1 mapped to WS.1.0. Page 0, 3, 9, 10, and 11 produced no matching WS readback change in this workspace. Cell 0 produced no WS.0.0 change; cells 1, 9, 10, 11, 60, and 61 mapped to zero-based WS cell indices 0, 8, 9, 10, 59, and 60. Readback proves stored integer and indexing behavior, not visual byte-channel rendering.
verification.restoreScript: SetCueCaptionColor 1,1,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 1,9,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 1,10,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 1,11,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 1,60,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 1,61,0xFF7D13; SetCueCaptionColor 2,1,0xFF0000

propertyMappingCoverage.notes: Runtime and object-tree evidence map indexed cue caption-color writes to WS.N.N.CaptionColor, where the first N is the zero-based page index and the second N is the zero-based cue index for pages and cells that exist in the loaded workspace. Focused-cue aliases such as ActGridFocusedCue.CaptionColor mirror the currently focused cue but are not the indexed target path.

SetEffectChannelAction.description: Set the effect-channel action intensity for a channel. BEYOND documentation says: 'Defines channel action parameter which impact channel calculation.' Current builds use parameter order `<value>, <index>`: value is a 0..100 channel-effect intensity, and index is 1..8 matching `Master.EffectChannelAction1..8` properties. verification.expectedCallback: Two-arg index sweep `(value=10+idx, idx=0..7)`: idx=1 → ch1=11, idx=2 → ch2=12, ..., idx=7 → ch7=17, ch8 untouched. idx=0 was silently dropped (no observable write to any channel). Subsequent `(88, 8)` set ch8=88. `(99, -1)` and `(77, 100)` silently dropped. Single-arg `SetEffectChannelAction 55` set ch1=55 and Master.EffectChannelAction (unindexed) = 55. SetFXAction.description: Set the action (morph) value for one layer. Action 0 is NOT the same as stopping; the effect still runs. Layer range is **1..8**. Writes to layers 4, 5, and 8 all landed on the corresponding `Master.FX<n>Action` property; writes to layer 9 were silently dropped. Older 1..4 documentation is stale, and the per-layer SetFXAction1..SetFXAction8 commands match the 1..8 range.

forms.description: Set effect action with morph between pre-effect and post-effect states.

parameters.name: layer
parameters.description: FX layer index. Range 1..8; out-of-range values are silently dropped (no parser error).

parameters.name: action
parameters.description: Morph percent.

verification.verificationScript:
ControlMaster
SetFXAction 4, 0.30
SetFXAction 5, 0.50
SetFXAction 8, 0.80
SetFXAction 9, 0.99
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against Master.FX<n>Action in BEYOND 2030. Baseline FX1..8.Action = 100, FX9.Action = 0. SetProp.description: Universal property setter; writes any BEYOND property by string path. Example: `SetProp "Master.bpm", 123`. For known properties, functionally equivalent to direct assignment (`Master.bpm = 123`). Useful when the property name is built dynamically from variables. The dispatched property write carries its own safety tier; treat as if the equivalent typed command (`SetBpm 123`) were inlined. The property-path string is **case-insensitive across the entire BEYOND property tree**. Unknown string property paths are **silently dropped** with no error or side effect (e.g. `SetProp "NotAProperty", 999` left existing properties unchanged). This unknown-path behavior is specific to SetProp's string path dispatch; direct expression reads or assignments of unknown properties can be BEYOND editor errors.

Case-insensitive: any combination of upper/lower case in the root or property segments resolves to the same target. Unknown string paths are silently no-op'd in SetProp dispatch - no runtime error, no Talk-bus diagnostic.

SetProp "MASTER.bpm", 150
SetProp "master.bpm", 160
SetProp "NotAProperty", 999
SetProp "Master.LCScrollSpeed", 7
SetProp "Master.lcscrollspeed", 5
SetProp "MASTER.LCSCROLLSPEED", 9
SetProp "master.lcScrollSpeed", 11
verification.expectedCallback: Probed via Talk UDP write + OSC readback against Master.BPM and Master.LCScrollSpeed in BEYOND 2030. (1) Master.BPM baseline = 120; SetProp variants `"Master.BPM"`, `"Master.bpm"`, `"MASTER.bpm"`, `"master.bpm"` produced 130, 140, 150, 160 respectively. (2) Master.LCScrollSpeed baseline = 3; SetProp variants `"Master.LCScrollSpeed"`, `"Master.lcscrollspeed"`, `"MASTER.LCSCROLLSPEED"`, `"master.lcScrollSpeed"` produced 7, 5, 9, 11 respectively. (3) `SetProp "NotAProperty", 999` left existing properties unchanged. Master.LCScrollSpeed has no typed PangoScript setter - only SetProp or direct assignment can write it - so its case-insensitivity verification proves the rule is general (not a quirk of Master.BPM going through SetBpm dispatch). Confirms case-insensitive resolution across the entire BEYOND property tree, plus silent-no-op for unknown paths.

StartCode.description: Start every script in the Code list whose CodeName matches. Asynchronous; caller does not block. Older documentation describes an overloaded multi-arg form (`StartCode "X", arg1, arg2,...`) that supposedly passes a parameter list to the called script. The parser **accepts** the multi-arg form (`StartCode "MyCode", 42` parses cleanly with no error), but the args are **silently discarded**; there is no receiving-side accessor exposed to PangoScript. Use the single-arg form for portable scripts; treat any extra args as a no-op until BEYOND adds a receiving-side API.

forms.description: Multi-arg form: parses but the args are silently discarded; there is no receiving-side accessor in current BEYOND despite older overloaded-parameter-list claims. Caller-side `StartCode "MyCode", 42` parses cleanly, but the receiver cannot read those values (`Arg1` raises 'Unknown function, undeclared or not initialized variable'; no `Arg*` / `Argv*` / `Param[N]` / `Sender` / `Caller` paths exist in BEYOND's Object Tree). Prefer the single-arg form until BEYOND ships a receiving-side parameter API.

parameters.description: Extra positional arguments. Parser accepts any number, but the values are **silently discarded** - no receiving-side accessor exists in current BEYOND.

verification.verificationScript:
// Caller side
StartCode "MyCode", 42
// Receiver side (separate script, fails to parse)
CodeName "EchoArgs"
var v
v = Arg1
OscOutTTS "/pangolint/echo/Arg1", "i", v
verification.expectedCallback: Multi-pronged probe in BEYOND 2030. (1) Caller parse: `StartCode "MyCode", 42` parses cleanly in the editor - no 'Code contain errors' popup. (2) Receiver parse: a receiver script with `var v / v = Arg1` raised 'Unknown function, undeclared or not initialized variable: arg1'. (3) Object Tree search: a search for Arg / Argv / Param / Sender / Caller / Self / Local identifiers returned only ProTrack.<n>.Param1..12 (FX layer params, unrelated to StartCode). (4) Editor Command list: searching 'startcode' surfaces only the single-arg example `StartCode "MyCode"`. Conclusion: caller-side parser accepts extra args but receiver-side parameter access is not implemented in current BEYOND. The multi-arg form is documented in the catalog as parser-valid-but-functionally-no-op so the editor doesn't false-flag it as a syntax error, but the description warns operators that the args are silently discarded.

StartFb4Discovery.description: Trigger an FB4 discovery scan and auto-reconnect any reachable FB4 hardware. The parameter is **ignored**: `StartFb4Discovery 0`, `StartFb4Discovery 1`, and bare `StartFb4Discovery` all produce identical behavior (reconnection within ~2.5s when reachable). Treat the command as effectively zero-arg. **Important sequencing**: this command does NOT reconnect FB4s by itself after `StopFb4Discovery`; that command both disconnects AND disables discovery. To restore a Stopped FB4, set `Fb4DiscoveryMode <0|1>` first (auto or always), then call `StartFb4Discovery`.

parameters.description: Optional placeholder; runtime ignores the value. Bare StartFb4Discovery is the preferred form. Provided for parser compatibility with existing scripts.

verification.verificationScript: StopFb4Discovery / wait FB4_XXXXX.Connected = 0 / Fb4DiscoveryMode 1 / StartFb4Discovery <arg> / poll FB4_XXXXX.Connected for reconnect
verification.expectedCallback: Disconnect-and-reconnect cycle against a connected FB4: StopFb4Discovery dropped FB4_XXXXX.Connected from 1 to 0 within ~100ms (FB3_XXXXX.Connected stayed at 1). With Fb4DiscoveryMode 1 set, all three argument forms (`0`, `1`, no-arg) reconnected the FB4 within ~2.5s - confirms the integer parameter is ignored. Without Fb4DiscoveryMode being set first (or after Fb4DiscoveryMode 0 + StartFb4Discovery 0 in an earlier probe), reconnection failed within 30+ seconds - Fb4DiscoveryMode 1 is the working setting in the observed setup. Discovery scan is fast on a local network with reachable hardware.

StopFb4Discovery.description: Disable FB4 auto-discovery and disconnect currently connected FB4 devices. Writes `FB4_<serial>.Connected` from 1 to 0 within about 100ms, and persistently disables discovery, meaning a subsequent `StartFb4Discovery` alone will NOT reconnect. Recovery requires `Fb4DiscoveryMode <0|1>` first to re-enable discovery, then `StartFb4Discovery`. FB3 devices use a different namespace and are unaffected. Calling mid-show kills laser output through every active FB4; not a routine operation.

verification.verificationScript: StopFb4Discovery / OscOutTTS "<reply>", "i", FB4_XXXXX.Connected
verification.expectedCallback: Disconnect verified at runtime: StopFb4Discovery dropped FB4_XXXXX.Connected from 1 → 0 within ~100ms (FB3_XXXXX.Connected stayed at 1, confirming the command is FB4-specific). Persistent disable-discovery side-effect verified: subsequent `StartFb4Discovery 0` and `StartFb4Discovery 1` standalone failed to reconnect within 15s each. Reconnection succeeded only after `Fb4DiscoveryMode 1` was issued first to re-enable discovery, then `StartFb4Discovery` (any form, since the integer arg is ignored).

SynchronizePlayerToBeat.description: Enable, disable, or toggle player-to-beat synchronization. BEYOND documentation says: 'Sets the global option for players to synchronize to the beat. **Synchronization occurs on player start and restart.** The idea is similar to quantize in audio software: it is nearly impossible to click exactly on the beat, so the timing will always be slightly off. This option corrects that by using the current sub-beat time as the alignment reference.' So this is a quantize-on-trigger behavior - players snap to beat at start/restart only, NOT continuous phase-lock. Standard checkbox 0/1/2 (off/on/toggle) convention; symbolic On/Off/Toggle also accepted.

UnLockScreen.description: Unlock the BEYOND UI - inverse of LockScreen. Zero-arg form unlocks the screen WITHOUT requiring the lock-screen password to be supplied. After `LockScreen` (with a UI-side password configured), bare `UnLockScreen` released `Status.Locked` from 1 back to 0. Notable security implication: script-driven unlocks bypass the UI password gate - operator-typed unlocks via the lock dialog still require the password, but Talk-bus / scripted unlocks do not. Pair this with TCP Talk Server `Password` auth (BEYOND.INI [General] TcpTalkServerPassword) if the deployment needs to gate scripted access.

verification.expectedCallback: With a UI-side password set in BEYOND's Configuration/Security, LockScreen drove Status.Locked from 0 → 1; subsequent bare UnLockScreen (zero-arg, no password supplied) released it back to 0. Confirms script-driven unlock bypasses the lock password.

Does NOT fire on Grid2 page changes (UI or scripted `SetGrid2Page`), and does NOT fire on `SetPage` (which is a no-op in current BEYOND 2030).

verification.verificationScript:
Brightness 100
WaitForPageChange
Brightness 1
verification.expectedCallback: Run as a waiter script alongside three trigger scripts (`SetGrid1Page 2`, `SetGrid2Page 2`, `SetPage 2`) plus UI clicks on each grid's page tabs. The LiveControl Brightness slider flipped from 100 to 1 only when Grid1's page changed (UI click on Grid1 page-2 tab; scripted `SetGrid1Page 2`). It did not flip on Grid2 page changes (UI click or scripted) or on `SetPage 2`. Confirms `WaitForPageChange` watches Grid1 page changes only.

WaitForTC.description: Suspend execution until BEYOND's currently-configured timecode source reaches the specified position. The source binding follows whatever is configured in BEYOND's TC panel: ArtNet, MIDI TC, LTC, or internal. Fourth argument is milliseconds (range 0..999); BEYOND converts incoming frame count to milliseconds using the source's framerate before comparing to the wait target.

forms.description: Wait for the specified timecode position on BEYOND's currently-configured TC source.

parameters.name: second
parameters.description: A value of 5 here unblocks the wait when the TC source reaches 5 seconds.

parameters.name: milliseconds
parameters.description: Milliseconds, not frames. `WaitForTC 0,0,0,500` targets roughly 0.5 seconds, which matches milliseconds but not frames-at-30fps (~16.7 s) or frames-at-25fps (out of range). Note: BEYOND uses ms here even though its TC sources transmit HH:MM:SS:FF on the wire - BEYOND converts the incoming frame count to ms using the source's framerate before comparing to the wait target.

verification.verificationScript:
Brightness 100
WaitForTC 0,0,5,0
Brightness 1
verification.expectedCallback: With Timecode Expert configured to send ArtNet TC to BEYOND and BEYOND set up to receive that ArtNet TC source, starting the generator from 00:00:00:00 caused the LiveControl Brightness slider to flip from 100 to 1 when the generator's TC reached 5 seconds. Confirms WaitForTC is bound to BEYOND's currently-configured TC source (ArtNet works) and that the third argument is seconds.

verification.verificationScript:
Brightness 100
WaitForTC 0,0,0,500
Brightness 1
verification.expectedCallback: Same ArtNet TC setup as above, generator started from 00:00:00:00. The LiveControl Brightness slider flipped from 100 to 1 near-immediately (within ~0.5 s of the start). Confirms the fourth argument is milliseconds, not frames - under the frames interpretation, 500 frames at 30 fps would have been ~16.7 s and at 25 fps would have been out of range.

propertyMappingCoverage.notes: Script wait primitive; it observes timecode but does not write a BEYOND Object Tree property.
